newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov blasts Belarus over journalist.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov blasts Belarus over journalist.

text.p: Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov attacked Belarus on Wednesday over its decision to annul a Russian journalist's credentials and vowed to defend press freedoms.
"The government will defend Russian journalists, wherever they work, be it Belarus, North Korea or Cuba," Nemtsov told a news conference.

He was commenting on a decision by the Belarussian Foreign Ministry earlier this week to withdraw the accreditation of Pavel Sheremet, the Minsk bureau chief of the Russian Public Television (ORT) company.
The ministry accused Sheremet of insulting and tendentious reporting from the country. He denied the charges.

"Pre-meditated misinterpretations of information on events in Belarus, insulting for the whole people of Belarus, are constantly repeated in reports by Pavel Sheremet," the press service said in a statement.
"The spreading of this tendentious material misinforms public opinion in Belarus and Russia."
Foreign reporters without accreditation may face legal problems in Belarus. They are also barred from attending official press conferences or interviewing government officials.

Nemtsov, seen as crictical of Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko's authoritarian policies, said the decision had gone against the letter of a Russian-Belarus accord on closer integration between the two Slav states.

The document, signed earlier this year, was watered down under pressure from Moscow liberals like Nemtsov to prevent Lukashenko playing a role in Russia's policy. A clause of the document called for press freedom in both states.
"We consider such actions absolutely impermissible," Nemtsov said. "First we will get explanations...then conclusions will be drawn. Russia has quite a variety of methods to protect its journalists."
Sheremet told Reuters on Tuesday he saw the ministry move as a renewal of pressure on the mass media in the republic.

In March, Belarus ordered a reporter for Russia's NTV television network to leave the country, first cancelling his accreditation. Lukashenko then accused foreign media, including Russian, of bias in reporting opposition protests.
The Belarussian leader is widely seen in the West as increasingly authoritarian, especially after he used a controversial referendum last year to crack down on the opposition and increase his powers.

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is generally more restrained on Belarus. He said he regretted the latest incident and even called it "outrageous", according to Interfax news agency. But he added Russia would make "no demarches".
